newsitem.title: USA: Crestar sees year 2000 costs at $22-27 mln.
newsitem.headline: Crestar sees year 2000 costs at $22-27 mln.

text.p: Crestar Financial Corp expects its year 2000 computer system compliance efforts will cost between $22 million and $27 million over the course of the project.

"We believe at this point, including the charge taken this quarter, that the costs will be in the neighborhood of $22-27 million over the next two and a half to three years," said Eugene Putnam, Crestar's senior vice president for investor relations.
In a statement announcing its second-quarter results, Crestar said it incurred about $4.3 million in costs during the quarter to deal with computer issues raised by the turning of the millennium.
Securities and Exchange Commission rules require companies to disclose separately the specific costs associated with the so-called "millennium bug" compliance if those costs are material in nature.
Putnam said work was scheduled to continue through the end of 1998, with the following year to be used "as a clean-up period."
